concerns.concern: Across all manipulations, T_c moves opposite to mobility, a known anticorrelation in gated KTO(111). A single trapped-charge/confinement variable could explain everything, so the PNR mechanism is not required. The review asks for T_c plotted against μ, R_s and n for all states.
concerns.quote: The data therefore look consistent with a single "hidden" variable: the trapped-charge or confinement state of the well, set by gate history and light.

concerns.concern: The authors do not discuss the established STO back-gating mechanism, in which electrons irreversibly escape over the well barrier into substrate traps on first sweeps. The review asks how this differs from the proposed picture.
concerns.quote: Discuss the established mechanism from STO back-gating: irreversible escape of electrons over the well barrier into substrate traps on first sweeps

concerns.concern: The dielectric measurement probes the whole 0.5 mm bulk substrate, not the nanometre-thick reduced interface layer. The loss peaks could be bulk impurity relaxations. Bare-substrate and varied-OV-density controls are needed.
concerns.quote: The dielectric measurement probes the 0.5 mm bulk substrate, not the interface.

concerns.concern: The dielectric response is measured in only one state. It should be measured in the virgin, gate-cycled and illuminated states, since PNR alignment should change it.
concerns.quote: If PNR alignment and randomization drive the memory, the dielectric response should change between these states. At present it is measured in only one state.

concerns.concern: Extrapolating the Arrhenius fits to the ~10³ s timescales of gate sweeps and relaxation gives temperatures well below 35 K and 95 K. The claimed coincidences are therefore quantitatively inconsistent, and ω₀ with uncertainties should be reported.
concerns.quote: Extrapolating the Fig. 3c fits to these frequencies gives characteristic temperatures noticeably below 35 K and 95 K

concerns.concern: The relaxation time τ is nearly constant from 10 to 180 K, which is incompatible with a 76 meV thermally activated process.
concerns.quote: The observed near-constancy is incompatible with relaxation limited by thermally activated PNR or OV processes.

concerns.concern: The fitted τ is comparable to the ~2×10³ s observation window, suggesting the single-exponential fits are window-limited. Longer windows, residuals and alternative fit forms are requested.
concerns.quote: This suggests the single-exponential fits are constrained by the window rather than by the physics.

concerns.concern: The ΔR/R₁ maxima at 35 K and 95 K each rest on a single, noisy data point. Repeats with finer temperature steps and reported temperature stability are needed.
concerns.quote: The ΔR/R₁ maxima at 35 K and 95 K (Fig. 4b) each rest on one data point.

concerns.concern: LED heating could thermally anneal the hysteresis. A dark thermal-excursion control is needed to show the light effect is photonic.
concerns.quote: A heating control is therefore essential: warm the sample in the dark to the maximum temperature reached under the LED

concerns.concern: Light characterization is missing: optical power and photon flux at the sample, flux dependence, wavelength dependence, and absorption of reduced KTO at 630 nm.
concerns.quote: LED optical power and photon flux at the sample

concerns.concern: There is no illumination effect at 2 K, and persistent photoconductivity appears only at ≥10 K. This contradicts the claim of activation at extremely low temperatures and suggests a thermally assisted process.
concerns.quote: This contradicts the statement (p. 4) that the processes "can be activated by red light illumination even at extremely low temperatures".

concerns.concern: Each erasure requires warming from the superconducting state to 10 K, so erasure does not operate in or near the superconducting regime.
concerns.quote: Erasure therefore does not operate in or near the superconducting regime.

concerns.concern: The "complete erasure" claim is not demonstrated: L0–L4 are compared only with each other, not with the virgin T_c curve and the baseline R_s.
concerns.quote: As shown, L0–L4 are compared only with each other.

concerns.concern: The authors note the system does not fully recover even at 180 K, which needs reconciling with the claim of complete erasure.
concerns.quote: The authors note the system does not fully recover even at 180 K. This also needs reconciling with "complete" erasure.

concerns.concern: The mechanism relies on 1–2% carrier-density changes extracted with a single-band Hall model in a multiband system. Subband mobility changes could produce such shifts with no change in total density. Full ρ_xy(B) curves, a two-band analysis and error bars are requested.
concerns.quote: If mobility ratios between subbands change, a single-band Hall n from ±6 T data can shift by this much with no change in total density.

concerns.concern: The carrier density is higher at −50 V than at +50 V, opposite to capacitive induction. This needs explicit explanation and a stated V_g sign convention.
concerns.quote: In Supp. Fig. 1c, n is *higher* at −50 V than at +50 V, opposite to capacitive induction.

concerns.concern: n and μ come from three separately prepared runs. Run-to-run reproducibility of the prepared state should be shown, and it should be shown that 6 T does not itself alter the dynamics.
concerns.quote: Please demonstrate run-to-run reproducibility of the prepared state.

concerns.concern: The first-cycle gate-current spike is orders of magnitude above displacement current, implying leakage or charge transfer through the substrate. The review asks for the sweep rate, the integrated charge compared with Hall Δn, and an integrated Q(V_g) loop.
concerns.quote: The first-cycle spike of about −10 nA near −50 V (Supp. Fig. 3a) is orders of magnitude above C·dV/dt.

concerns.concern: The −15 V onset in Supplementary Note 3 and the −17 V threshold in Fig. 2g are inconsistent and should be reconciled.
concerns.quote: The −15 V onset in Supp. Note 3 and the −17 V threshold in Fig. 2g should be reconciled.

concerns.concern: There is no direct evidence of PNR alignment or remnant polarization; the picture is only a schematic. P–E/Q–V loops, ε after poling, or SHG/Raman are requested.
concerns.quote: There is no direct evidence of PNR alignment or remnant polarization.

concerns.concern: T_c should be measured after Type A versus Type B end states. The apparent sign dependence looks more like internal gating than alignment strengthening pairing.
concerns.quote: Fig. 1e suggests sign dependence, which looks more like internal gating than "alignment strengthens pairing".

concerns.concern: The ΔL ∝ ε correlation is weak evidence: both are monotonic in T, and generic trap filling also scales with ε. The 35 K kink is drawn by eye over a narrow range. Error bars and a comparison with a generic trap-filling model are requested.
concerns.quote: Both ΔL and ε are monotonic in T, so they will correlate whatever the mechanism.

concerns.concern: It is unclear which frequency's ε is used for the ΔL comparison, given that the process is quasi-static. The non-standard notation "ε∞" should be defined.
concerns.quote: State which frequency's ε is used, given that the process is quasi-static.

concerns.concern: Novelty must be explicitly positioned against Ref. 30, which already reported cryogenic gate-cycle T_c enhancement, room-temperature recovery and coexisting ferroelectricity.
concerns.quote: The abstract's "previously unrecognized interplay" needs explicit positioning against it.

concerns.concern: All data appear to come from one device. Reproducibility on additional samples, ideally with different oxygen-vacancy content, is needed.
concerns.quote: All data appear to come from one device.

concerns.concern: T_c shifts are only about 0.02–0.07 K but are given without error bars.
concerns.quote: Please add error bars on T_c; the shifts are only about 0.02–0.07 K.

concerns.concern: Retention of the gate-imprinted state at 1.4 K and 10 K over hours is not quantified, and the full thermal reset temperature is not stated.
concerns.quote: Please quantify retention of the gate-imprinted state at 1.4 K and 10 K over hours.

concerns.concern: That the activation energy is smaller than the photon energy does not imply photons drive PNR or OV processes; an optical transition with appreciable cross-section is needed.
concerns.quote: This requires an optical transition with appreciable cross-section, not merely sufficient energy.

concerns.concern: The "deep donor states" are not identified. Photo-ionized donors should increase scattering, yet mobility rises, and it is not stated whether the centres lie within the 2DEG's scattering range.
concerns.quote: Photo-ionizing deep donors leaves positively charged centres that should scatter more strongly. Explain why μ nonetheless increases.

concerns.concern: The claim that excess electrons tunnel back into deep donor states beyond −17 V has no independent support.
concerns.quote: The claim that excess electrons "tunnel back into deep donor states" beyond −17 V (p. 6) has no independent support.

concerns.concern: The neuromorphic and quantum-memristor application claims are overstated, given ~7% T_c tunability, 10²–10⁴ s erasure times and operation only at T ≥ 10 K.
concerns.quote: The neuromorphic and quantum-memristor framing in the abstract and conclusion should be tempered, or supported with figures of merit.

concerns.concern: Stated reasons for the 35 K line are inconsistent: TO-mode softening onset versus the PNR peak temperature. Peak 1 "near 30 K" is compared with 35 K.
concerns.quote: The Fig. 3 caption says the 35 K line marks the onset of TO-mode softening.

concerns.concern: The Fig. 3d caption says ΔL deviates above 35 K, while the text says it is steeper below.
concerns.quote: The Fig. 3d caption says ΔL "deviates above"; the text says "steeper below".

concerns.concern: It should be stated where the gate current is sensed, since coax and stray capacitance matter at high T where the sample capacitance is only tens of pF.
concerns.quote: State where I_g is sensed.

concerns.concern: The low-T ε (~1500–2000) is well below the bulk KTO value of ~4000, and ε shows a slight downturn below ~10 K at 0.1 Hz. Both need comment on geometry, fringing or electrode effects.
concerns.quote: The low-T ε of about 1500–2000 is well below the bulk KTO literature value of about 4000.

concerns.concern: The Methods rationale linking fringe effects to the van der Pauw transport geometry is unclear, and the FEM correction magnitude is not given.
concerns.quote: Specify the FEM correction magnitude.

concerns.concern: The number of cycles needed for the loops to stabilize is given as "3~4" in Supplementary Note 1 but four in the main text.
concerns.quote: Supp. Note 1 says loops stabilize in "3~4" cycles; the main text says four. Harmonize.

concerns.concern: Text and labelling errors: a duplicated sentence, "laser emitting diode", multiple typos, a wrong R_s label in Supplementary Note 4, "Extended Figure 5", inconsistent units, and a wrong figure citation.
concerns.quote: Supp. Note 4, item 2, labels 856 Ω as R_s^b; it should be the elevated value R_s^a.
